chunks.rationale: test/threadView.test.tsx #607 cases are the contract: (1) A→null→B remount plus a late scroll at scrollTop=0 must still pin; (2) a permission card that grows after the first pin, then a late scroll, must pin to the new scrollHeight. The older #408 cases still prove ResizeObserver follows growth while stuck and does not yank a user who scrolled up.
risks: jsdom has no layout, so the tests fake clientHeight/scrollHeight/scrollTop. They cannot prove Chrome overflow-anchoring; that is why .body also sets overflow-anchor: none.
forceStick is only armed on a real thread recovery/switch or a new pendingPermission.requestId — the #408 'scrolled up' case is initial mount and must keep unsticking.

chunks.rationale: src/components/ThreadView.tsx pinIfStuck + useLayoutEffect + onBodyScroll. Stick used to clear when Chrome fired a delayed scroll after the #83 loading-gap remount or after a tall permission/plan/question card landed. forceStick re-pins those events until a pin actually moves scrollTop onto the bottom; pinning.current ignores the scroll event we ourselves caused.
risks: If pinIfStuck never moves scrollTop (flex unconstrained, distance always 0) forceStick stays true and a later user scroll-up would be treated as layout noise and re-pinned. ResizeObserver on the body viewport is the intended release when real overflow appears.
A new permission requestId force-sticks even if the user had scrolled up to copy something. That is the product intent for a blocking prompt; a question/plan prompt shares the same requestId path.

chunks.rationale: ThreadView.module.css .body overflow-anchor: none stops Chrome from adjusting scrollTop when a card is inserted at the bottom. ResizeObserver now also re-attaches when pendingPermission or isWorking change so the new sibling (card / working strip) is observed.
risks: overflow-anchor: none is global for the transcript. That is what we want for chat pinning; it does not affect nested scrollers (plan body, code blocks).
Not verified in a live Electron window — renderer tests plus tsc only. The race is Chromium-specific (async scroll + overflow anchoring + flex remount).
This is the center transcript (.body), not AgentsPanel's right-rail .scroll. If the report was about the Environment/Agents tab keeping scroll across threads, that is still open.
